title: Evaluating Language Models on Cross-Language Code Functional Equivalence
abstract: arXiv:2608.23961v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Background: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance across a variety of code-understanding tasks, leading many to believe that they can reason about program semantics. However, existing evaluations primarily focus on single-language settings or rely on synthetically generated code, raising concerns about whether current results reflect true semantic understanding. Aims: We investigate whether LLMs can accurately judge functional equivalence across different programming languages in human-written code, a setting that requires deeper reasoning beyond superficial similarity. Method: We introduce PolyHuman, a dataset of human-written programs in CPP, Java, and Python. Using this dataset, we evaluate intra- and inter-language equivalence detection across open-weight and proprietary LLMs, selecting GPT-o4-mini as a representative model to assess stability. We then manually analyze 81 cases of systematic disagreement

translated_title: 评估语言模型在跨语言代码功能等价性上的表现
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.23961v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：背景：大型语言模型（LLMs）在各种代码理解任务中表现出色，使许多人相信它们能够推理程序语义。然而，现有评估主要集中于单语言设置或依赖合成生成的代码，这引发了对当前结果是否反映真正语义理解的担忧。目的：我们研究LLMs是否能准确判断人类编写代码中不同编程语言之间的功能等价性，这种设置需要超越表面相似性的更深层推理。方法：我们引入了PolyHuman数据集，包含CPP、Java和Python的人类编写程序。利用该数据集，我们评估了开放权重和专有LLMs在语言内部和跨语言等价性检测上的表现，并选择GPT-o4-mini作为代表性模型来评估稳定性。然后，我们手动分析了81个系统性分歧案例。
tldr: 本研究提出PolyHuman数据集，评估LLMs在人类编写的跨语言代码功能等价性判断中的表现，并发现模型在该任务中存在系统性分歧，揭示其语义推理的局限性。
en_tdlr: This study introduces the PolyHuman dataset to evaluate LLMs' performance on judging functional equivalence across human-written code in different languages, revealing systematic disagreements that highlight limitations in semantic reasoning.
